spec.description: Earthquakes from the USGS feed over the last 30 days, with who lives nearby.

options.content:
### Where the data comes from

- **Earthquakes**: the [USGS real-time feed](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/geojson.php) of the last 30 days, read straight from USGS by your browser when the dashboard opens. *PAGER alert*, *intensity (MMI)*, *felt reports* and *tsunami* are USGS's own assessments, published only for the earthquakes that warrant one. Public domain (U.S. Government).
- **Populated places**: [Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/) 1:10m populated places (v5.1.2), about 7,300 towns and cities with population estimates. Public domain.

### How "people within 100 km" is counted

For every earthquake of magnitude 4.5 or more, the populations of the Natural Earth places within 100 km of the epicentre are added up; that is the figure *Most exposed* ranks by. The *People within 100 km* total counts each place once, however many of the filtered earthquakes it is near, and *Selected earthquake* gives the figure for any magnitude. It uses each place's city-proper figure, not its metropolitan area, so a metro area listed as several places is not counted twice. It leaves out everyone living outside those places, so **read it as a lower bound**, not as USGS's PAGER exposure estimate.

### How it works

Both datasets are loaded once into DuckDB running in your browser (the Chaski data source). Every filter and click is answered there, without a round trip to the server.

spec.description: Every earthquake the filters leave, by magnitude and depth: the depth axis stretches the shallow kilometres, where most quakes are, and stops at 300 km like the depth filter. Drawn by Mosaic from the same dataset.
spec.title: Depth and magnitude

options.spec:
params:
  quakeFilters: { select: crossfilter }
plot:
  - mark: dot
    data: { from: quakes, filterBy: $quakeFilters }
    x: mag
    y: depth_axis
    r: 1.6
    fill: '#FF9830'
    fillOpacity: 0.35
    stroke: none
xDomain: Fixed
yDomain: [0, 300]
yScale: sqrt
yReverse: true
yTicks: [0, 10, 35, 70, 150, 300]
xLabel: Magnitude →
yLabel: ↓ Depth (km)
marginLeft: 40

spec.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "Earthquakes"
FROM $quakes
WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $__crossfilter($quakeFilters)

spec.description: Every filter on the earthquakes, each counted under the others: brush a histogram, or draw an area on the map. A × clears one, Clear all clears them all.
spec.title: Filters

options.content:
**Click an earthquake** on the map, or a row in *Most exposed*, to see who lives near it.

**Drag** across the bars in *Filters*, **draw** an area on the map, move the map's **time slider**, or **play** the timeline under the map: every panel follows, answered in your browser.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT id, time, latitude, longitude, mag, depth, greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) AS depth_axis, place, alert
FROM $quakes
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)

SELECT name, country, latitude, longitude, pop_max
FROM $places
WHERE pop_max >= 100000

spec.description: Earthquakes of the last 30 days from the USGS feed, sized by magnitude, over populated places from Natural Earth. Drag the time slider or draw an area to filter the rest of the dashboard; click an earthquake to see who lives near it.
spec.title: Earthquakes and populated places

spec.rawSql:
WITH f AS (
  SELECT q.* FROM $quakes AS q
  WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $__crossfilter($quakeFilters)
)
SELECT f.place AS "Place",
       round(f.mag, 1) AS "Mag",
       coalesce(f.alert, 'none') AS "PAGER",
       e.people_100km AS "People ≤100 km",
       e.largest_place AS "Largest place",
       e.largest_pop AS "Population",
       f.id, f.latitude, f.longitude
FROM f JOIN $exposure AS e ON e.id = f.id
WHERE e.people_100km > 0
ORDER BY e.people_100km DESC
LIMIT 10

WITH f AS (
  SELECT q.* FROM $quakes AS q
  WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $__crossfilter($quakeFilters)
),
strong AS (SELECT latitude, longitude FROM f WHERE mag >= 4.5),
near AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT p.name, p.latitude, p.longitude, p.pop_min
  FROM strong AS q
  JOIN $places AS p
    ON p.latitude BETWEEN q.latitude - 1 AND q.latitude + 1
   AND least(abs(p.longitude - q.longitude), 360 - abs(p.longitude - q.longitude))
       <= 1 / greatest(cos(radians(q.latitude)), 0.01)
  WHERE 2 * 6371 * asin(sqrt(
  power(sin(radians(p.latitude - q.latitude) / 2), 2)
  + cos(radians(q.latitude)) * cos(radians(p.latitude))
    * power(sin(radians(p.longitude - q.longitude) / 2), 2))) <= 100
)
SELECT coalesce(sum(pop_min), 0)::DOUBLE AS "People within 100 km" FROM near

spec.description: People living in towns and cities within 100 km of any of the filtered earthquakes of magnitude 4.5 or more, each place counted once however many of them it is near. Counted from Natural Earth's populated places (city proper, not metro areas), so it leaves out rural areas: read it as a lower bound.
spec.title: People within 100 km

spec.rawSql:
WITH q AS (SELECT latitude, longitude FROM $quakes WHERE id = $quake),
     candidates AS (
       SELECT p.name AS "Place", p.country AS "Country", p.pop_min AS "Population",
              2 * 6371 * asin(sqrt(
  power(sin(radians(p.latitude - q.latitude) / 2), 2)
  + cos(radians(q.latitude)) * cos(radians(p.latitude))
    * power(sin(radians(p.longitude - q.longitude) / 2), 2))) AS km
       FROM q, $places AS p
       WHERE p.latitude BETWEEN q.latitude - 1 AND q.latitude + 1
     )
SELECT "Place", "Country", "Population", round(km) AS "Distance (km)"
FROM candidates
WHERE km <= 100
ORDER BY "Population" DESC
LIMIT 15

SELECT q.place AS "Place",
       strftime(q.time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', '%d %b %H:%M UTC') AS "Time",
       round(q.mag, 1) AS "Magnitude",
       round(q.depth) AS "Depth (km)",
       coalesce(q.alert, 'none') AS "PAGER alert",
       q.mmi AS "Intensity (MMI)",
       q.felt AS "Felt reports",
       CASE WHEN q.tsunami = 1 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Tsunami",
       (SELECT coalesce(sum(p.pop_min), 0)::DOUBLE
          FROM $places AS p
         WHERE p.latitude BETWEEN q.latitude - 1 AND q.latitude + 1
           AND 2 * 6371 * asin(sqrt(
  power(sin(radians(p.latitude - q.latitude) / 2), 2)
  + cos(radians(q.latitude)) * cos(radians(p.latitude))
    * power(sin(radians(p.longitude - q.longitude) / 2), 2))) <= 100) AS "People within 100 km",
       q.url AS url
FROM $quakes AS q
WHERE q.id = $quake

source.sql:
SELECT
  f.id AS id,
  to_timestamp(f.properties.time / 1000) AS time,
  f.geometry.coordinates[2]::DOUBLE AS latitude,
  f.geometry.coordinates[1]::DOUBLE AS longitude,
  f.geometry.coordinates[3]::DOUBLE AS depth,
  -- Depth clamped to the histogram's axis, so the depth filter and its bars agree.
  greatest(least(f.geometry.coordinates[3]::DOUBLE, 299.9), 0) AS depth_axis,
  f.properties.mag::DOUBLE AS mag,
  f.properties.place::VARCHAR AS place,
  f.properties.alert::VARCHAR AS alert,
  f.properties.mmi::DOUBLE AS mmi,
  f.properties.felt::INTEGER AS felt,
  f.properties.tsunami::INTEGER AS tsunami,
  f.properties.sig::INTEGER AS sig,
  f.properties.url::VARCHAR AS url
FROM read_json('https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/summary/all_month.geojson'), unnest(features) AS t(f)
WHERE f.properties.mag IS NOT NULL

SELECT
  f.properties.name::VARCHAR AS name,
  f.properties.adm0name::VARCHAR AS country,
  f.properties.latitude::DOUBLE AS latitude,
  f.properties.longitude::DOUBLE AS longitude,
  f.properties.pop_min::BIGINT AS pop_min,
  f.properties.pop_max::BIGINT AS pop_max
FROM read_json('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/v5.1.2/geojson/ne_10m_populated_places_simple.geojson'), unnest(features) AS t(f)
WHERE f.properties.pop_min > 0

WITH q AS (
  SELECT id, latitude, longitude FROM $quakes WHERE mag >= 4.5
),
near AS (
  -- A band of about 111 km around each quake first, so the distance runs on
  -- a few candidates instead of every place on Earth. The longitude band
  -- widens with latitude and wraps at the antimeridian.
  SELECT q.id, p.name, p.pop_min, p.pop_max,
         2 * 6371 * asin(sqrt(
           power(sin(radians(p.latitude - q.latitude) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(q.latitude)) * cos(radians(p.latitude))
             * power(sin(radians(p.longitude - q.longitude) / 2), 2)
         )) AS km
  FROM q
  JOIN $places AS p
    ON p.latitude BETWEEN q.latitude - 1 AND q.latitude + 1
   AND least(abs(p.longitude - q.longitude), 360 - abs(p.longitude - q.longitude))
       <= 1 / greatest(cos(radians(q.latitude)), 0.01)
)
SELECT q.id,
       -- DOUBLE, not BIGINT: DuckDB promotes SUM(BIGINT) to HUGEINT, which
       -- DuckDB-WASM serializes as a part-indexed object, not a JS number, in
       -- any consumer that sums this column across rows.
       coalesce(sum(n.pop_min) FILTER (WHERE n.km <= 100), 0)::DOUBLE AS people_100km,
       count(n.name) FILTER (WHERE n.km <= 100) AS places_100km,
       arg_max(n.name, n.pop_max) FILTER (WHERE n.km <= 100) AS largest_place,
       max(n.pop_max) FILTER (WHERE n.km <= 100) AS largest_pop
FROM q
LEFT JOIN near AS n ON n.id = q.id
GROUP BY q.id
